candidates.basis: fcstm_model.text root block `[*] -> UnspecifiedInitial;`; inspection_equivalent_facts.states show UAVSwarmStateMachine reachable_from_initial=false; verify_facts.non_proved reachability:state:UAVSwarmStateMachine:line:8 status=refuted; NL-CONTRACT-NL2-DERIVED-d8dfe5954980b6dba9e3 owner=root/system scope, target=target search state.
candidates.expected: The UAV swarm's overall/root operating scope must have an exact default-entry edge that reaches the operating hierarchy containing the target-search state (Searching), matching the author-source `[*] -> Searching` inside UAVSwarmStateMachine.
candidates.observed: The closed FCSTM text shows `[*] -> UnspecifiedInitial` at the outer root (llms_emp_feedback_final_0006), and a separate `[*] -> Searching` only inside UAVSwarmStateMachine (transition:line:23). Because the outer root's only initial edge targets UnspecifiedInitial (a synthetic leaf with no outgoing edge), UAVSwarmStateMachine itself is never entered from the true root, so the inner `[*] -> Searching` edge, though present and correctly targeted, is never exercised from the top-level initial entry. inspection_equivalent_facts confirms state:UAVSwarmStateMachine reachable_from_initial=false and verify_facts refutes reachability:state:UAVSwarmStateMachine:line:8.
candidates.reason: NL2's derived initial_entry contract requires the UAV swarm's overall operating scope to have an initial entry into the target-search operating state. The closed model's outer root only enters a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial leaf, never the UAVSwarmStateMachine composite that owns Searching; this is a genuine missing default-entry edge at the exact owner scope required by the contract, distinct from and not repaired by the satisfied inner [*]->Searching edge.
candidates.requirement_quote: Before the mission is completed, the UAV swarm continuously performs target search tasks, during which it operates within three different state areas.
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: The inner `[*] -> Searching` edge inside UAVSwarmStateMachine is itself present and correctly targeted (transition:line:23, S2-satisfiable), so if the contract's owner is read narrowly as 'UAVSwarmStateMachine scope' rather than the outer root scope, that local edge alone would satisfy an owner-local initial_entry obligation; this candidate specifically targets the outer/root-level entry gap that prevents UAVSwarmStateMachine from ever being entered.
candidates.title: Root scope has no default entry into UAVSwarmStateMachine/Searching

candidates.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.states Searching/Intercepted/FormationAdjustment reachable_from_initial=false; verify_facts.non_proved reachability checks for state:Searching:line:19, state:Intercepted:line:20, state:FormationAdjustment:line:9 all status=refuted; exact_source_inventory tr_0002/tr_0008 confirm author intent for this exact chain.
candidates.expected: Upon interception, the UAV swarm's current operating state (Searching) must transition to the formation adjustment state (FormationAdjustment), and this relation must be part of the machine's actually reachable behavior.
candidates.observed: The exact edges Searching->Intercepted (transition:line:24, trigger Interception_Detected) and Intercepted->FormationAdjustment (transition:line:26) both exist with correct source/target identities matching the author source (tr_0002, tr_0008). However neither endpoint state is reachable from the true top-level initial entry: inspection_equivalent_facts marks Searching, Intercepted, and FormationAdjustment all reachable_from_initial=false, and verify_facts refutes their reachability checks.
candidates.reason: While S2 endpoint identity for Searching->Intercepted->FormationAdjustment is exact and matches author intent, the contract's operative obligation ('must_reach') is undermined because the entire scope containing these states is unreachable from the true root; this is a precise but not S2-expressible operational gap (S2 only checks edge existence, not reachability), so it is preserved as predicate-null W1 rather than silently omitted.
candidates.requirement_quote: When the UAV swarm is intercepted, it transitions to the formation adjustment state.
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: The endpoint pair itself (Searching->Intercepted->FormationAdjustment) is structurally exact and correctly targeted; if this contract is read purely as a local edge-existence obligation, it is satisfied and only the separate root reachability defect above applies. This candidate is included because the same defect chain makes the interception behavior operationally void, which a structure-contrast lens should flag alongside (not instead of) the satisfied local endpoints.
candidates.title: Searching->Intercepted->FormationAdjustment endpoints exist but the whole chain is unreachable from root

candidates.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers row for Interception_Detected (reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]); inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for Interception_Detected; verify_facts.non_proved event-consumer:Interception_Detected status=refuted.
candidates.expected: The interception event must be accepted (consumed) somewhere reachable within the UAV swarm's mission-active operating scope.
candidates.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers lists Interception_Detected with consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:24] but reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] (empty); diagnostics include EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for Interception_Detected; verify_facts refutes event-consumer:Interception_Detected.
candidates.reason: The derived event_consumer_coverage contract requires the interception event be accepted wherever it can occur within the operating scope; exact deterministic facts show the sole declared consumer is structurally present but unreachable, which is the precise negative fact for this property. No frozen predicate directly states reachable event-consumer coverage, so predicate_id remains null while the candidate is preserved for W1.
candidates.requirement_quote: When the UAV swarm is intercepted, it transitions to the formation adjustment state.
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: The consumer transition (Searching->Intercepted, transition:line:24) is declared and structurally correct; a reviewer could argue the NL only requires structural existence of the interception-handling transition, which is present. This candidate targets the stronger reachable-consumer property that the contract's own coverage direction (must_occur/unconsumed) requires and that the exact facts refute.
candidates.title: Interception_Detected has a declared consumer but no reachable consumer

response.reason: This lens compares the NL-derived transition-group, endpoint, containment, and event-consumer obligations against the exact author-source and closed FCSTM structure. Root cause across NL3, NL4, and the derived contracts is the same: the closed FCSTM top-level machine `UAVSwarmStateMachine` has no default-entry edge from the outer root, so the entire operating hierarchy (Searching/Intercepted/FormationAdjustment/AdjustingFormation/Attack/AttackingTarget) is unreachable from `[*]`, even though every author-intended endpoint (Searching->Intercepted->FormationAdjustment, Searching->Attack) is structurally present with correct source/target identities. This lens surfaces the structural root-entry gap plus its consequences on reachability/coverage contracts, while explicitly not converting satisfied endpoint/action facts into false wrong-target or dead-end claims.

cardinality_bindings.alternative_reading: concurrent_regions: 'state areas' could denote simultaneously active orthogonal partitions rather than sequential child states, though no explicit parallel/orthogonal region language or separator exists in the supplied NL or PlantUML source to establish this as primary.
cardinality_bindings.basis: NL2 quote 'it operates within three different state areas'; exact_source_inventory.states shows UAVSwarmStateMachine has exactly three direct child states/composites: Searching, FormationAdjustment, Attack (Intercepted is a fourth direct child not part of the three areas per NL framing, so some ambiguity remains about which three); canonical_source_ir.model.concurrent_regions count=0 indicating no explicit region separators exist in source.
cardinality_bindings.reason: NL2 states the UAV swarm 'operates within three different state areas' during target search, but supplied NL/source semantics do not fix a single primary member domain. A plausible primary reading is direct_child_states of UAVSwarmStateMachine (Searching, FormationAdjustment, Attack are its three direct children per exact_source_inventory.states, matching the count of 3), which is a strong candidate for direct_child_states. However, 'state areas' could also competently be read as concurrent_regions if the NL intends parallel operating zones, though nothing in the NL or source explicitly establishes orthogonal/parallel region semantics (no separators, no explicit parallel-region language), so concurrent_regions is not clearly established either. Because the generic phrase 'state areas' does not unambiguously commit to one domain type over the other without over-reading, and because selecting a domain must not be driven by matching the observed count, this lens records the primary as direct_child_states with concurrent_regions as an explicit alternative_reading rather than collapsing to a single unambiguous exact reading.

output.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability, event-consumer operational coverage, dead-end/frontier facts, and termination stability. The FCSTM shows the entire semantically-meaningful UAVSwarmStateMachine subtree (Searching, Intercepted, FormationAdjustment, AdjustingFormation, Attack, AttackingTarget) is structurally unreachable from the true root, because the root's only initial edge ([*] -> UnspecifiedInitial) targets a synthetic leaf state with zero outgoing transitions, while UAVSwarmStateMachine itself has no incoming edge from any reachable state. This single root-level defect causally explains why every downstream state_action, transition-endpoint, and event-consumer contract is operationally unreachable, but per protocol each is preserved as its own atomic candidate against its own contract rather than collapsed into one. NL2's initial-entry derived contract, NL3/NL4 event-consumer derived contracts, and NL4's deadlock/action contract are all impacted independently. Cardinality (three state areas) is handled via the required cardinality_bindings row.

decisions.reason: The NL requirement quote 'it operates within three different state areas' is bound to the composite UAVSwarmStateMachine (state:UAVSwarmStateMachine:line:8) via CARD-BIND-NL2-1. The closed author-source inventory (llms_emp_feedback_final_0006.puml lines 2,4,7,10,16) establishes exactly four direct child states: FormationAdjustment (line:9), Attack (line:14), Searching (line:19), and Intercepted (line:20), confirmed by the ModelIR containment facts and the two bound transitions (line:23, line:24) and event Interception_Detected (line:3). Under the primary direct_child_states reading this is a precise 4-vs-3 cardinality mismatch (violation_direction=extra), which is established by the complete finite inventory even though predicate_id is null and the backend is unsupported (a W-boundary fact, not a D defeater). However, a competent alternative member-domain reading exists in which the three named mission-phase states (Searching, FormationAdjustment, Attack) are read as the 'three different state areas' referenced by the NL text, treating Intercepted as a reactive/interrupt state rather than one of the three primary areas; this alternative is supported by the same exact source/model facts (the distinct semantic role of Intercepted as an interception-triggered branch reached via the bound transitions and event) and is not excluded by any exact supplied contract text specifying which member domain governs the count. This alternative therefore survives as an undercutting defeater at the D1 boundary rather than being defeated, since no exact clause forecloses the named-members reading.
decisions.strongest_defeater: An alternative competent reading treats 'three different state areas' as referring to the three named operating states/composites the swarm transitions through during its mission (Searching, FormationAdjustment, Attack) as an explicit_named_members domain, excluding the reactive Intercepted state as a transient interrupt handler rather than a primary 'state area'; under this member-domain reading the count could be 3 rather than 4, so the exact required member domain remains ambiguous between direct_child_states and explicit_named_members.
decisions.violated_obligation: NL-CONTRACT-NL2-DERIVED-f3027d1b791038b6be9e requires that UAVSwarmStateMachine realize exactly 3 state areas within the UAV swarm target-search operating scope (per the NL requirement 'it operates within three different state areas'), counted under the primary direct_child_states reading of the composite.

issues.basis: fcstm_model.text root block `[*] -> UnspecifiedInitial;`; inspection_equivalent_facts.states show UAVSwarmStateMachine reachable_from_initial=false; verify_facts.non_proved reachability:state:UAVSwarmStateMachine:line:8 status=refuted; NL-CONTRACT-NL2-DERIVED-d8dfe5954980b6dba9e3 owner=root/system scope, target=target search state.
issues.expected: The UAV swarm's overall/root operating scope must have an exact default-entry edge that reaches the operating hierarchy containing the target-search state (Searching), matching the author-source `[*] -> Searching` inside UAVSwarmStateMachine.
issues.observed: The closed FCSTM text shows `[*] -> UnspecifiedInitial` at the outer root (llms_emp_feedback_final_0006), and a separate `[*] -> Searching` only inside UAVSwarmStateMachine (transition:line:23). Because the outer root's only initial edge targets UnspecifiedInitial (a synthetic leaf with no outgoing edge), UAVSwarmStateMachine itself is never entered from the true root, so the inner `[*] -> Searching` edge, though present and correctly targeted, is never exercised from the top-level initial entry. inspection_equivalent_facts confirms state:UAVSwarmStateMachine reachable_from_initial=false and verify_facts refutes reachability:state:UAVSwarmStateMachine:line:8.
issues.reason: NL2's derived initial_entry contract requires the UAV swarm's overall operating scope to have an initial entry into the target-search operating state. The closed model's outer root only enters a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial leaf, never the UAVSwarmStateMachine composite that owns Searching; this is a genuine missing default-entry edge at the exact owner scope required by the contract, distinct from and not repaired by the satisfied inner [*]->Searching edge.
issues.requirement_quote: Before the mission is completed, the UAV swarm continuously performs target search tasks, during which it operates within three different state areas.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The inner `[*] -> Searching` edge inside UAVSwarmStateMachine is itself present and correctly targeted (transition:line:23, S2-satisfiable), so if the contract's owner is read narrowly as 'UAVSwarmStateMachine scope' rather than the outer root scope, that local edge alone would satisfy an owner-local initial_entry obligation; this candidate specifically targets the outer/root-level entry gap that prevents UAVSwarmStateMachine from ever being entered.
issues.title: Root scope has no default entry into UAVSwarmStateMachine/Searching

However neither endpoint state is reachable from the true top-level initial entry: inspection_equivalent_facts marks Searching, Intercepted, and FormationAdjustment all reachable_from_initial=false, and verify_facts refutes their reachability checks.
issues.reason: While S2 endpoint identity for Searching->Intercepted->FormationAdjustment is exact and matches author intent, the contract's operative obligation ('must_reach') is undermined because the entire scope containing these states is unreachable from the true root; this is a precise but not S2-expressible operational gap (S2 only checks edge existence, not reachability), so it is preserved as predicate-null W1 rather than silently omitted.
issues.requirement_quote: When the UAV swarm is intercepted, it transitions to the formation adjustment state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The endpoint pair itself (Searching->Intercepted->FormationAdjustment) is structurally exact and correctly targeted; if this contract is read purely as a local edge-existence obligation, it is satisfied and only the separate root reachability defect above applies. This candidate is included because the same defect chain makes the interception behavior operationally void, which a structure-contrast lens should flag alongside (not instead of) the satisfied local endpoints.
issues.title: Searching->Intercepted->FormationAdjustment endpoints exist but the whole chain is unreachable from root

The exact root-level owner therefore has no functioning path that ever reaches Searching.

issues.title: No owner-local root edge realizes entry into Searching (target search) because the owning composite itself is unreachable

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.states Searching outgoing_transition_refs=[transition:line:24,transition:line:25]; inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING (UnspecifiedInitial line 7); verify_facts.checks deadlock:state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:7 status=refuted, outgoing_count=0.
issues.expected: The UAV swarm must remain in ongoing flight operation from which entry into the attack state is triggered upon receiving task assignment information; the operating state must not be a dead end.
issues.observed: Searching (the in-flight operating state) has exact outgoing transitions (transition:line:24, transition:line:25) so it is not itself a local dead end. However, the only state actually reachable from the true root besides the root itself is UnspecifiedInitial, which inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics flags as LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING and verify_facts.checks confirms deadlock:state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:7 status=refuted (i.e., it truly has zero outgoing transitions), making the actual reachable execution frontier a dead end before any in-flight behavior can occur.
issues.reason: Following the explicit frontier rule that a synthetic placeholder's zero-outgoing fact remains only supporting initial-entry evidence and that an unreachable state with outgoing edges is not a deadlock violation, this candidate is retained only as a predicate-null W1 observation flagging that the exact reachable execution frontier terminates at a genuine dead end (UnspecifiedInitial) before the NL4 in-flight progress obligation can ever be exercised, rather than asserting Searching itself is a dead end.
issues.requirement_quote: During flight, if task assignment information is received, it enters the attack state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Per frontier discipline, an unreachable state with exact outgoing continuation is not itself a deadlock violation; the genuine dead-end fact belongs to UnspecifiedInitial, a compiler-owned synthetic placeholder, whose zero-outgoing fact must not become a separate deadlock_freedom issue unless the source contract establishes it as an operating state, which NL4 does not for UnspecifiedInitial itself.
issues.title: In-flight/Searching operating state has exact outgoing continuation but the operating scope containing it is unreachable, and the true reachable leaf is a genuine dead end
